claim: CloudFront caches copies of your content close to viewers in edge locations and regional edge caches. For files that are not cached there, it keeps persistent connections with your origin servers so the files are fetched as quickly as possible.
question: How does CloudFront provide higher performance, for cached and for not-cached files?

values.display: persistent connections with your origin servers

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudFront employs a global network of edge locations and regional edge caches that cache copies of your content close to your viewers.

For files not cached at the edge locations and the regional edge caches, Amazon CloudFront keeps persistent connections with your origin servers so that those files can be fetched from the origin servers as quickly as possible.

note: FAQ item 5; feeds the FAQ quick-fire section.

claim: CloudFront collapses simultaneous viewer requests at an edge location for the same file into a single request to your origin server, which reduces the load on your origin servers.
question: How does CloudFront reduce the load on the origin when many viewers ask for the same file at the same time?

values.display: a single request to your origin server

qualifiers.scope: same file, at one edge location
qualifiers.condition: viewer requests that arrive at the same time

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudFront also uses techniques such as collapsing simultaneous viewer requests at an edge location for the same file into a single request to your origin server.
This reduces the load on your origin servers reducing the need to scale your origin infrastructure, which can bring you further cost savings.

claim: When the origin is an AWS origin such as Amazon S3 or Amazon EC2, AWS no longer charges for data transfer out to CloudFront. This applies to data transfer from all AWS Regions to all global CloudFront edge locations.

claim: For every origin in a CloudFront distribution you can assign a backup origin that automatically serves your traffic if the primary origin is unavailable. You choose which HTTP 4xx/5xx status codes returned from the primary origin trigger the failover, and the two origins can be any combination of AWS and non-AWS origins.
question: How does CloudFront provide origin redundancy, and what triggers the failover to the backup origin?

values.display: any combination of AWS and non-AWS origins

qualifiers.scope: per origin of a CloudFront distribution

evidence.quote: For every origin that you add to a CloudFront distribution, you can assign a backup origin that can be used to automatically serve your traffic if the primary origin is unavailable.
You can choose a combination of HTTP 4xx/5xx status codes that, when returned from the primary origin, trigger the failover to the backup origin.
The two origins can be any combination of AWS and non-AWS origins.

claim: Regional edge caches sit between your origin web server and the edge locations that serve viewers. They have a larger cache width than any individual edge location, so objects remain cached longer and CloudFront goes back to the origin less often.

between your origin webserver and AWS edge locations

evidence.quote: Regional Edge Caches have a larger cache width than any individual edge location, so objects remain cached longer.
They are located between your origin webserver and AWS edge locations that serve content directly to your users.
